NAME

md_docs_2networking-runtime - Connection ownership and execution

network_connection_t owns a transport, framing state, deadlines, and connection security storage. network_server_t owns listeners, accepted connections, and their execution workers. Media servers, ACDS, and native session hosts supply application callbacks through the same interface.

TCP uses the platform event loop. WebSocket and WebRTC keep their respective library event engines. Backend adapters deliver input to the common connection executor; modes do not accept sockets, run transport receive loops, or maintain synthetic TCP registry entries for other transports.

network_connection_open() resolves and establishes an outbound endpoint. Its optional configuration carries the caller's timeout and cancellation callback/data through TCP and WebSocket establishment; application shutdown is checked as well. network_connection_run() drives packet callbacks on its controlling worker. An established authenticated peer can be adopted by a server or an outbound owner without repeating the peer's cryptographic negotiation.

Application callbacks

Callback Ownership contract open Allocate application state and attach it to the connection. A failure still enters teardown. Packet Types Borrow the decoded payload until return. Return a terminal protocol/application error to close. closing Stop and join application producers before transport destruction. Must permit retry after a failed join. closed Release application state after transport callbacks have drained. Called once.

Hooks for one connection execute serially, outside backend event loops. A failed join retains the connection, transport, application state, and owning server so shutdown can retry safely. Owners must join their execution worker before destroying an outbound connection.

Registry visits snapshot and pin connections under the registry mutex, then invoke callbacks after releasing it. Connection teardown removes the registry entry and waits for existing visitors before releasing application state. A visitor may request a stop; it must not synchronously destroy its pinned owner.

Protocol and media behavior

The media and discovery negotiation profiles preserve their existing wire protocols. They share execution, admission, deadlines, and teardown. Transport security and authenticated peer adoption remain explicit inputs to negotiation; neither replaces required password or identity authentication.

Discovery participants use the same media path after either TCP establishment or authenticated WebRTC adoption. Initial capabilities precede stream startup for both; there is no separate client-join announcement or TCP-only wait loop.

Native clients, discovery participants, and servers accept --webrtc-bind-address IP (ASCII_CHAT_WEBRTC_BIND_ADDRESS) to select the local IPv4 or unbracketed IPv6 address for ICE UDP sockets. Discovery gathers all interfaces when this option is empty. Servers otherwise use their selected TCP interface. The signaling service's address does not select the ICE interface. For a call between two processes on the same machine, set this option to 127.0.0.1 on both peers to keep connectivity checks on loopback. This also avoids host firewall or local-network permissions affecting loopback tests. tests/python/integration/discovery/test_discovery_webrtc.py verifies both selected ICE candidates and received media; --Audio additionally verifies stereo packet sizes, and --ipv6 selects IPv6 loopback for ICE while signaling stays on IPv4.

Server render workers submit media directly to the ACIP outbound scheduler. That scheduler owns congestion admission, ordered control traffic, media dropping, and encryption sequencing for every transport. There is no second mode-owned audio queue, video send buffer, or transport send thread.

Windows validation

test-network-connections exercises TCP, WebSocket, and local WebRTC callbacks, pinned registry visits, rejected startup, handshake and partial-packet deadlines, malformed input, and retained cleanup after a failed producer join. The other standalone suites cover participant ownership, peer readiness, security policy, backend events, and congestion.

The media server allocates slots and buffers only after security negotiation and initial capabilities succeed. Unauthenticated stalled peers consume a bounded connection entry rather than a media slot.

The media server sends SERVER_STATE when security becomes ready, before waiting for capabilities. Browser discovery uses that announcement to begin application setup; it must not depend on allocating a media slot first.

tests/integration/network_fps_windows.py uses real native servers and ConPTY clients. It measures the CLI presentation counter over a sustained interval for TCP, WebSocket, and WebRTC, retaining commands, logs, terminal output, and JSON samples. A connected socket or render-loop log is insufficient to pass.

web/web/playwright.networking.config.ts starts an isolated web server and runs unified-networking.spec.ts against native processes built from this checkout. The browser checks advancing rendered frames and disconnect/reconnect behavior, with screenshots and traces retained as evidence.
